name: Nanamica
why: Tokyo label from 2003 that puts GORE-TEX into a Balmacaan and a blazer, the Goldwin company behind The North Face Purple Label; one US store, Wooster Street.
origin: Founded in 2003 in Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan by Eiichiro Homma (Founder / Creative Director per brand about page) and Goldwin's securities report records Goldwin establishing 株式会社ナナミカ in March 2003.

notes.tech: Thread proposed 4 (2026-10-11): GORE-TEX (2L, incl. Cotton GORE-TEX co-developed with Gore Japan), WINDSTOPPER, PERTEX UNLIMITED, PRIMALOFT Black, CORDURA, COOLMAX EcoMade, ALPHADRY (Goldwin), KODENSHI down, MURON recycled nylon — licensed (Gore, Pertex, PrimaLoft, Invista/Cordura, The LYCRA Company, KODENSHI); ALPHADRY is developed by parent Goldwin (group-owned, not nanamica-owned); Cotton GORE-TEX fabric co-developed with Gore Japan; share of range 44/115 styles (38%) name a branded technical fabric in title or composition. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): nanamica names no owned factory, no clothing maker and no clothing mill on its own pages, and only 2 of 115 clothing styles state a country of origin. What it documents is fabric engineering (licensed GORE-TEX, COOLMAX and the like, which is tech, not craft) and one process, its loopwheel COOLMAX jersey; that lifts it off a 1 but does not reach a 3, which needs named makers or mills. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

craft_evidence.owned: none stated: nanamica site names no owned factory; company profile lists design/manufacture/sale but no plant (parent Goldwin facilities not checked)
craft_evidence.makers: mostly none: REGAL (Regal Walker last) named on the footwear collaboration pages; Spiber named as fibre maker on 2 Brewed Protein styles; clothing pages name no sewing factory ("an overcoat factory in Japan", "a domestic blanket factory in Japan", unnamed)
craft_evidence.mills: none on clothing pages (115 read via feed); Sanyo Leather tannery named on the 2 footwear pages; "shuttle looms in Okayama" on bags, mill unnamed
craft_evidence.madein: 2/115 clothing styles state a country (2 OOAL Graphic Tees 24SS: China) plus 1 coat "made at an overcoat factory in Japan"; feed read in full
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: nanamica inc. founded March 2003, Shibuya, Tokyo (company profile); nanamica USA Inc. founded May 2019, NYC
craft_evidence.process: partial: Loopwheel jersey documented (loopwheel machines over half a century old, ~1 m of fabric per hour); Cotton GORE-TEX co-development and GORE testing described; otherwise fabric descriptions only
craft_evidence.reasoning: nanamica names no owned factory, no clothing maker and no clothing mill on its own pages, and only 2 of 115 clothing styles state a country of origin. What it documents is fabric engineering (licensed GORE-TEX, COOLMAX and the like, which is tech, not craft) and one process, its loopwheel COOLMAX jersey; that lifts it off a 1 but does not reach a 3, which needs named makers or mills.

ownership.owner: Goldwin Inc. (TSE 8111) holds 96.7% of 株式会社ナナミカ (nanamica inc.; CEO Takeshi Nomura, capital JPY 60m); nanamica USA Inc. 100% (indirect) per Goldwin 有価証券報告書
